items.title: Sumner Labat Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: Dick Allen introduces himself as the interviewer ('I'm Dick Allen. There's my name. That's so the people that hear this will know.') and asks questions; the interviewee (Sumner Labat) responds to the questions but does not describe a personal or professional relationship with Dick Allen beyond the i

ctx.x: Let's see. Today is November the 11th, isn't it? What is it? Yes, I want to see. Yeah, November the 11th, 1962. And I'm here. I don't even know where I am. You better tell me where I'm at. Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. And what's the street we're on, the address? 309 Esther Brook Street. Esther Brook Street in Bay St. Louis, yes. And could I get both of you's names? Sure. I'm Carmen, and he is Sumner Labatt. Sumner Labatt. And Carmen Labatt. And you're a man and wife? That's right. I've been for 41 years. 41 years.…

I guess about, let me see, they had two trumpets, three trumpets, one baritone, one bass, snag drum, bass drum, and two trombones. How many pieces? How many pieces you didn't come to? I didn't come to that. That's about eight. Did you say tuba or no?
